key_insight: Embedding deep image features as a manifold enables geometry-aware spectral matching that reduces noisy semantic correspondences.
engineering_relevance: The work applies finite-element discretisation to image correspondence, rather than developing an FEM surrogate for solid mechanics.
method: Construct an image manifold from deep features.
Use Galerkin finite elements to derive a discrete Laplace–Beltrami operator for spectral functional maps.
Use a neural adjoint map to represent nonlinear correspondences.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art zero-shot results on multiple dense correspondence benchmarks of real-world images, without quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Applicability to solid-mechanics simulation or FEM surrogate modelling is not demonstrated in the abstract.
paper_title: Manifold Embedding of Deep Image Features for Image Matching via Neural Adjoint Maps
